QUESTION: Does the SEARCH-ARCHITECTURE BRANCH beat the VALIDATED BASELINE at the owner's shape and 2000 ms — and what does the depth ration cost the one-turn search that pays for it? This is the merge decision for claude/cluster-lookahead, not a flag's promotion.
ARMS: baseline  |  search-arch
ARM CONFIGS — A CROSS-BRANCH PAIR: one bundle per arm, from the refs below.
--arm 'baseline=<bundle-baseline>'
--arm 'search-arch=<bundle-search-arch>'
BUNDLES — build one per arm, from the ref named here, and record the
resolved SHA from each bundle.json in findings.md:
tools/simworker/build-bot.sh origin/claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg <bundle-baseline> --fetch
baseline: claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg — baseline
tools/simworker/build-bot.sh origin/claude/cluster-lookahead <bundle-search-arch> --fetch
search-arch: claude/cluster-lookahead — feature
READS OUT: deepestPlies, deepBranches, depthEffectRate, worstWallMs, decisions, score, sharePar

DESIGN NOTE: RESPECIFIED 20260830 AS A BRANCH-VERSUS-BRANCH VALIDATION, under the owner's branching ruling of the same day (docs/BRANCHING.md). THE ARMS ARE TWO BUNDLES FROM TWO REFS, both running their shipped defaults with no bot config on either side: `baseline` is built from origin/claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg, the validated baseline; `search-arch` is built from origin/claude/cluster-lookahead, the search-architecture feature branch, whose default bot carries the deep layer AND the cluster enumeration always-built. WHAT THIS DISSOLVES: the question this row carried until today was 'does the default bot keep carrying two never-raced features, or do they become config fields defaulting off until a sweep promotes them?'. Under the ruling there is no default to argue about — the accumulated architecture lives on a feature branch and the branch either MERGES on this evidence or it does not. The pending owner decision recorded on this row and on CENTAUR_CLUSTER_ENUM's is answered by the paradigm rather than by a status edit. WHAT IT COSTS, SAID OUT LOUD: the previous shape (`default` against `depthless` = bot={"depth":{"plyCap":0}}) was a one-variable pair — same bundle, same evaluator, same bounds, differing only in how far the search could look — and this one is not. Two branch tips differ by everything that landed on either since they forked, so a delta here attributes to THE BRANCH and to nothing finer. That is the correct instrument for a MERGE decision and the wrong one for a mechanism claim, and the two must not be confused in the write-up. The one-variable depth pair remains available on the feature bundle alone and is the follow-up if the branch arm reads positive and somebody wants to know which part of it did the work. AND READ THE RATE FOR WHAT IT IS: the 30% and 22.5% figures on the feature branch are DISAGREEMENT rates — how often removing depth would stage a different move — measured on 11x11 two-team piece boards. They are not improvement and they are not the owner's board; src/lobster/__tests__/DEPTH-NUMBERS.md is the committed record of what each figure measures, and the owner-shape rates (mixed-king 2/24, snake5-queen 5/24) are measured by the `depth-effect rate at the owner's shape` block of src/lobster/__tests__/depth-acceptance.test.ts. Their replay quality signal came back EMPTY — all seven disagreements replay identical same-turn ledgers — which is precisely why this live sweep is the instrument and the probes are not.

MERGE DECISION: THIS EXPERIMENT IS THE MERGE DECISION FOR claude/cluster-lookahead. A `search-arch` arm that clears the verified A/A floor on the batch's own metrics merges into claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg and is recorded VALIDATED. An arm that does not clear it does not merge; the branch stays a retained parallel test arm and the reason is written into findings.md. Neither outcome is a status word in this file's schema — the schema judges evidence about flags, and a branch merge is a judgement about a branch — so it is recorded here, in prose, where a reader meets it.

GATE: deepestPlies > 0 and deepBranches > 0 on the `search-arch` arm, on at least the piece-bearing cells. ZERO THERE IS A BROKEN ARM AND MUST BE REPORTED AS A REFUSAL, NOT AS A NULL — it means the bundle was built from the wrong ref, or the deep layer never opened a thread on these boards, and either way the pair measured something other than what it is named for. Record the resolved SHA of both bundles from bundle.json in findings.md: a branch-versus-branch verdict that quotes branch names and not SHAs is a claim nobody can reproduce.

REQUIRES: ONE BUNDLE PER ARM, BUILT FROM THE REF NAMED IN THE BUNDLES BLOCK, AND NO BOT CONFIG ON EITHER. The cross-branch shape is the harness's normal case, not an extension of it: build-bot.sh resolves any git ref to a bundle, and run-pair.js launches the arms at the same instant in separate processes and pairs them afterwards by gameId. Batch 1 ran exactly this shape in P1 — `integrated` @ 66904d2 against `perf-substrate` @ 8059b86, 144 games paired, 0 dropped, 0 pairing problems. DO NOT PASS bot= ON EITHER ARM. The baseline bundle predates the 20260829 flag teardown and has no src/lobster/bot-config module, so checkContenders would REFUSE the spec (correctly) the moment a contender declared one; with no bot config declared, nothing calls requireBundleTakesBotConfig and both arms simply play their shipped bots, which is the comparison this experiment is for. ENGAGEMENT IS READ ON THE search-arch ARM ONLY, from belief.deepestPlies / deepBranches on the per-game rows. The baseline arm is engagement-verified BY CONSTRUCTION — the deep layer is not in that build at all, so there is no counter to read and no silent-A/A risk on that side; the failure mode P5 taught (an arm that names a treatment and quietly does not run it) can only live on the search-arch side, which is where the gate below points.
HOW AN ARM IS SELECTED HERE, AND WHY THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT. This is a
BRANCH-VERSUS-BRANCH pair under the branching paradigm (docs/BRANCHING.md,
owner ruling 20260830): an architecture change is built on its own branch,
validated as a batch arm, and MERGED on the result. So the arms are two
BUNDLES built from two refs, each running its own shipped default, and the
BUNDLES block above is the whole of the arm definition.
DO NOT ADD bot= TO EITHER ARM unless this spec prints one. A bundle built
from a pre-teardown ref has no src/lobster/bot-config module, and
checkContenders refuses a spec that declares a bot config against it —
correctly, because such a bundle would ignore the config and play its
shipped bot under the arm's name. With no config declared, that check does
not fire and both arms simply play what they ship, which is the comparison.
READ THE VERDICT AT THE RIGHT GRAIN. Two branch tips differ by everything
that landed on either since they forked, so a delta attributes to THE
BRANCH and to nothing finer. That is the right instrument for a merge
decision and the wrong one for a mechanism claim.
